Post-filtering ten globally nearest items yields an expected 0.1 matching items if independent filter selectivity is 1%; it can often return none despite valid matches elsewhere. Overfetching helps but becomes expensive and still lacks a fixed recall guarantee. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.09320)

Blindly restricting graph traversal to allowed nodes can disconnect useful paths. Filter-aware HNSW/ACORN-style methods separate traversal from result eligibility or add connectivity strategies, while very selective filters may favor an exact scan of the filtered subset. [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.08281)

Use metadata-aware search with explicit recall tests across selectivities and correlation between filters/geometry. Permission filters must be enforced before returning content; traversal access and user-visible result authorization are distinct. Benchmark update behavior and filtered ground truth, not only unfiltered ANN recall.
